**IN THE MATTER OF THE ESTATE OF TEODORO R. FONSECA, DECEASED**
Los Angeles County Superior Court, Probate Division Case No. 22STPB09714
Effective Date: April 28, 2023
**SETTLEMENT STANDSTILL AGREEMENT**
This Settlement Standstill Agreement (this \"**Agreement**\") is entered into as of April 28, 2023 (the \"**Effective Date**\"), by and among the following parties:
**MARGUERITE D. FONSECA** (\"**Petitioner**\"), an individual residing at 1847 Coldwater Canyon Drive, Beverly Hills, California 90210, the surviving spouse of the Decedent (as defined below);
and

**RAFAEL T. FONSECA**, an individual residing at 502 Olive Avenue, Unit 3, Burbank, California 91502; **ISABELA C. FONSECA-GREER**, an individual residing at 78 Eucalyptus Lane, Santa Monica, California 90402; and **NICOLÁS R. FONSECA**, an individual residing at 1190 Elm Street, Apt. 4B, Palo Alto, California 94301 (collectively, the \"**Contestants**\"), adult children of the Decedent from a prior marriage.
Petitioner and Contestants are sometimes referred to herein individually as a \"**Party**\" and collectively as the \"**Parties**.\"
**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, Teodoro R. Fonseca (the \"**Decedent**\") died intestate on September 3, 2022, while a resident of Los Angeles County, California, leaving an estate of substantial value comprised of real property, interests in limited liability companies, financial accounts, an intellectual property portfolio, and personal property;

**WHEREAS**, Marguerite D. Fonseca, the surviving spouse of the Decedent, filed a Petition for Letters of Administration on October 5, 2022, in the Los Angeles County Superior Court, Probate Division, and the petition was assigned Case No. 22STPB09714 (the \"**Proceeding**\");

**WHEREAS**, Rafael T. Fonseca, Isabela C. Fonseca-Greer, and Nicolás R. Fonseca, adult children of the Decedent from a prior marriage to the late Cecilia R. Fonseca, filed an initial objection to the Petition for Letters of Administration on November 14, 2022, challenging, among other things, the appointment of Petitioner as administrator of the Estate and disputing the community property characterization of certain Estate assets;

**WHEREAS**, Contestants filed an amended objection on January 9, 2023, adding claims regarding the existence and enforceability of a premarital agreement allegedly executed by the Decedent and Petitioner on May 30, 2008, and asserting that certain media-related assets, including the Decedent\'s interests in Lumiére Canyon Studios LLC and Pacific Rim Narrative Partners LLC, constitute the Decedent\'s separate property;
**WHEREAS**, Petitioner is represented by Calderwood & Harkness LLP (Howard Quinn, Esq., Responsible Partner), with offices at 350 South Grand Avenue, Suite 4800, Los Angeles, California 90071;

**WHEREAS**, Contestants are represented by Brennan, Ortega & Saldívar LLP (Damian R. Ortega, Esq., Lead Attorney), with offices at 1900 Avenue of the Stars, Suite 2100, Los Angeles, California 90067;

**WHEREAS**, on March 10, 2023, the Parties stipulated to mediation before the Honorable Constance Adler (Ret.) of the Westside Dispute Resolution Center, located at 11400 West Olympic Boulevard, Suite 550, Los Angeles, California 90064, for the purpose of exploring the potential resolution of the disputes in the Proceeding;

**WHEREAS**, on March 22, 2023, the Parties further stipulated to the appointment of Ashford Fiduciary Services Inc. (Gerald Whitmore, Principal Officer), with offices at 600 Wilshire Boulevard, Suite 1450, Los Angeles, California 90017, as the neutral administrator of the Estate pending resolution of the dispute (the \"**Neutral Administrator**\"), and the Court entered an order approving such appointment on March 24, 2023;

**WHEREAS**, a mediation session was conducted on April 12, 2023, before the Honorable Constance Adler (Ret.), at the offices of the Westside Dispute Resolution Center, which session, while productive in narrowing certain issues, did not result in a full resolution of the dispute between the Parties;

**WHEREAS**, the Parties recognize that the Proceeding involves complex issues relating to the characterization of marital and separate property, the validity and enforceability of the alleged premarital agreement, the valuation of closely held business interests, and individual claims asserted by certain Contestants, and that a meaningful resolution of these issues will require additional time, investigation, information exchange, and negotiation;

**WHEREAS**, the Parties now desire to enter into this Settlement Standstill Agreement to pause active litigation in the Proceeding, toll all applicable deadlines, preserve the status quo of the Estate, and create a structured framework for continued settlement negotiations in the interest of reaching an amicable resolution;

**WHEREAS**, the estimated probate estate is valued at approximately Seventy-One Million One Hundred Twelve Thousand Dollars (\$71,112,000) per Petitioner\'s preliminary estimate, or approximately Sixty-Eight Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$68,750,000) per Contestants\' preliminary estimate, comprising, among other assets, the Decedent\'s interests in Lumiére Canyon Studios LLC and Pacific Rim Narrative Partners LLC, real property located in Beverly Hills and Malibu, financial accounts held at Veltara Basin Bank, N.A., an intellectual property portfolio, and personal property, all as more particularly described in Exhibit A attached hereto; and

**WHEREAS**, the Parties believe that a period of standstill and continued negotiation is in the best interests of all Parties and the Estate, and will promote the efficient administration and preservation of Estate assets during the pendency of settlement efforts.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the forbearances and commitments of the Parties contained in this Agreement, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged by each Party, the Parties agree as follows:
**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article I shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

**Section 1.1 --- \"Agreement.\"** \"Agreement\" means this Settlement Standstill Agreement, including all exhibits attached hereto and all amendments, supplements, or modifications hereto made in accordance with Section 7.5.
**Section 1.2 --- \"Parties.\"** \"Parties\" means, collectively, Petitioner and Contestants. \"Party\" means any one of them individually.

**Section 1.3 --- \"Petitioner.\"** \"Petitioner\" means Marguerite D. Fonseca, an individual residing at 1847 Coldwater Canyon Drive, Beverly Hills, California 90210, the surviving spouse of the Decedent and the petitioner in the Proceeding.

**Section 1.4 --- \"Contestants.\"** \"Contestants\" means, collectively, (a) Rafael T. Fonseca, an individual residing at 502 Olive Avenue, Unit 3, Burbank, California 91502; (b) Isabela C. Fonseca-Greer, an individual residing at 78 Eucalyptus Lane, Santa Monica, California 90402; and (c) Nicolás R. Fonseca, an individual residing at 1190 Elm Street, Apt. 4B, Palo Alto, California 94301, each an adult child of the Decedent from a prior marriage, and the contestants in the Proceeding.
**Section 1.5 --- \"Court.\"** \"Court\" means the Los Angeles County Superior Court, Probate Division, or any successor court having jurisdiction over the Proceeding.

**Section 1.6 --- \"Proceeding.\"** \"Proceeding\" means Case No. 22STPB09714, *In re Estate of Teodoro R. Fonseca, Deceased*, pending in the Court, together with any and all motions, petitions, objections, claims, counterclaims, cross-petitions, and other matters filed or pending therein.

**Section 1.7 --- \"Estate.\"** \"Estate\" means the probate estate of Teodoro R. Fonseca, Deceased, including all assets, rights, interests, claims, and obligations comprising the probate estate, as more particularly described in Exhibit A hereto.

**Section 1.8 --- \"Neutral Administrator.\"** \"Neutral Administrator\" means Ashford Fiduciary Services Inc., a California corporation, with its principal office at 600 Wilshire Boulevard, Suite 1450, Los Angeles, California 90017, Gerald Whitmore serving as Principal Officer, appointed by the Court as the neutral administrator of the Estate pursuant to the Stipulation for Appointment of Neutral Administrator filed March 22, 2023, and the Court\'s order entered March 24, 2023.

**Section 1.9 --- \"Mediator.\"** \"Mediator\" means the Honorable Constance Adler (Ret.), serving through the Westside Dispute Resolution Center, located at 11400 West Olympic Boulevard, Suite 550, Los Angeles, California 90064.

**Section 1.10 --- \"Standstill Period.\"** \"Standstill Period\" means the period commencing on the Effective Date and ending on the Expiration Date, as such Expiration Date may be extended pursuant to Article V of this Agreement.
**Section 1.11 --- \"Effective Date.\"** \"Effective Date\" means April 28, 2023, which is the date on which this Agreement becomes effective upon execution by all Parties.

**Section 1.12 --- \"Initial Expiration Date.\"** \"Initial Expiration Date\" means October 28, 2023, which is six (6) calendar months from the Effective Date. References to the \"Expiration Date\" shall mean the Initial Expiration Date or, if this Agreement has been renewed pursuant to Section 5.2, the then-applicable expiration date following such renewal.

**Section 1.13 --- \"Settlement Discussions.\"** \"Settlement Discussions\" means any and all communications, whether oral, written, or electronic, between or among the Parties, their respective counsel, the Mediator, or any other person participating in settlement negotiations at the direction of the Parties, relating to the potential resolution, compromise, or settlement of the Proceeding or any claims, disputes, or issues arising therein, including all proposals, counterproposals, term sheets, draft agreements, memoranda, position statements, and other materials prepared in connection with such negotiations.

**Section 1.14 --- \"Petitioner\'s Counsel.\"** \"Petitioner\'s Counsel\" means Calderwood & Harkness LLP, with offices at 350 South Grand Avenue, Suite 4800, Los Angeles, California 90071, Howard Quinn, Esq. serving as the Responsible Partner.

**Section 1.15 --- \"Contestants\' Counsel.\"** \"Contestants\' Counsel\" means Brennan, Ortega & Saldívar LLP, with offices at 1900 Avenue of the Stars, Suite 2100, Los Angeles, California 90067, Damian R. Ortega, Esq. serving as the Lead Attorney.
**[ARTICLE II --- TOLLING OF LITIGATION DEADLINES AND STANDSTILL OBLIGATIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Tolling of Deadlines.** Effective as of the Effective Date and continuing for the duration of the Standstill Period, all litigation deadlines in the Proceeding shall be tolled. The deadlines subject to tolling under this Section include, but are not limited to, deadlines for filing responsive pleadings, motions, amended pleadings, petitions, objections, and other papers; deadlines for propounding and responding to discovery, including interrogatories, requests for production of documents, requests for admission, and deposition notices; deadlines for pretrial submissions, including witness lists, exhibit lists, and pretrial statements; and any other deadlines imposed by the California Code of Civil Procedure, the California Probate Code, the California Rules of Court, the local rules of the Los Angeles County Superior Court, or any order of the Court. Upon the termination or expiration of this Agreement, all such tolled deadlines shall recommence with the same number of days remaining as existed on the Effective Date. For the avoidance of doubt, if a Party had ten (10) days remaining to file a responsive pleading as of the Effective Date, such Party shall have ten (10) days from the date of termination or expiration of this Agreement to file such responsive pleading.

**Section 2.2 --- Prohibition on New Filings.** During the Standstill Period, no Party shall file any new motion, petition, objection, amended pleading, cross-petition, claim, or other pleading or paper in the Proceeding without the prior written consent of all other Parties, except as expressly permitted under Section 2.4 of this Agreement. Any filing made in violation of this Section 2.2 shall be deemed a breach of this Agreement, and the non-breaching Party or Parties shall be entitled to seek all available remedies, including but not limited to a motion to strike the improperly filed pleading and an award of attorneys\' fees and costs incurred in connection with addressing such breach.

**Section 2.3 --- Prohibition on discovery.** During the Standstill Period, no Party shall serve, propound, or issue any discovery in connection with the Proceeding without the prior written consent of all other Parties. The prohibition set forth in this Section 2.3 extends to, but is not limited to, interrogatories, requests for production of documents, requests for admission, deposition notices (whether for oral or written deposition), subpoenas duces tecum, subpoenas for testimony directed at third parties, and any other form of formal or informal discovery under the California Code of Civil Procedure or applicable rules. Nothing in this Section 2.3 shall prohibit the voluntary exchange of information between the Parties\' counsel in connection with Settlement Discussions, provided that any such voluntary exchange shall be subject to the confidentiality provisions of Article IV.

**Section 2.4 --- Permitted Actions.** Notwithstanding the prohibitions set forth in Sections 2.2 and 2.3 of this Agreement, the following actions are expressly permitted during the Standstill Period without the prior consent of any other Party:

> \(a\) Filings that are required to preserve jurisdictional or statutory rights of any Party that cannot be tolled by private agreement of the Parties, including but not limited to any filing necessary to prevent the loss of standing or the running of a non-waivable statutory period;

> \(b\) Filings that are necessary to protect the Estate from imminent dissipation, waste, loss of value, or destruction of Estate assets, provided that the filing Party shall provide the other Parties with at least forty-eight (48) hours\' prior written notice of its intent to make such filing, except in circumstances where such notice is impracticable due to the emergent nature of the threat;

> \(c\) Filings required to comply with any court order entered prior to the Effective Date that, by its terms, requires action during the Standstill Period, including but not limited to the Court\'s order of March 24, 2023, approving the appointment of the Neutral Administrator;

> \(d\) Joint stipulations or agreed orders submitted by all Parties for the Court\'s consideration and approval, including stipulations extending or modifying deadlines, stipulations relating to the Neutral Administrator, and stipulations relating to the administration of the Estate;

> \(e\) Filings related to the ongoing administration of the Estate by the Neutral Administrator in the ordinary course of its duties, including accountings, inventories, reports, and fee applications, provided that such filings are consistent with the terms of this Agreement and the Stipulation for Appointment of Neutral Administrator.

**Section 2.5 --- Preservation of Claims and Defenses.** Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as a waiver, release, abandonment, or prejudice of any claim, defense, right, or remedy of any Party in the Proceeding or otherwise. All claims, defenses, rights, and remedies of the Parties as of the Effective Date are expressly reserved and preserved in full, including but not limited to all claims and defenses identified in Exhibit B attached hereto. The entry into this Agreement shall not create any estoppel, laches defense, or other impediment to any Party\'s assertion of any claim or defense upon the termination or expiration of this Agreement.

**Section 2.6 --- Statute of Limitations.** The Parties agree that any statute of limitations, statute of repose, prescriptive period, or other time-based legal defense or time bar applicable to any claim asserted or that could be asserted in the Proceeding, or arising out of or relating to the same facts, circumstances, transactions, or occurrences at issue in the Proceeding, shall be tolled for the duration of the Standstill Period. Each Party agrees not to assert the expiration of any such time-based defense as a bar to any claim to the extent that such expiration occurred during the Standstill Period and would not have occurred but for the tolling provided by this Section 2.6. This Section 2.6 shall be given the broadest possible construction consistent with applicable law in order to effectuate the Parties\' intent to preserve all claims and defenses during the Standstill Period.
**[ARTICLE III --- CONTINUED NEUTRAL ADMINISTRATION OF THE ESTATE]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Continuation of Neutral Administrator.** Ashford Fiduciary Services Inc. shall continue to serve as the Neutral Administrator of the Estate during the Standstill Period, in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Stipulation for Appointment of Neutral Administrator filed with the Court on March 22, 2023, the Court\'s order approving such appointment entered on March 24, 2023, and any supplemental court orders issued in connection therewith. The Neutral Administrator\'s duties and obligations under this Agreement are in addition to, and not in limitation of, the duties and obligations set forth in the Stipulation and the Court\'s order. In the event of any conflict between the terms of this Agreement and the terms of the Stipulation or Court order, the Court\'s order shall control.

**Section 3.2 --- Scope of Administration.** During the Standstill Period, the Neutral Administrator shall exercise its fiduciary duties in a prudent and commercially reasonable manner and shall, at a minimum, perform the following functions:
> \(a\) **Maintenance and Preservation of Estate Assets.** Maintain, preserve, protect, and safeguard all Estate assets, including but not limited to:

> \(i\) Real property located at 1847 Coldwater Canyon Drive, Beverly Hills, California 90210 (the \"Beverly Hills Residence\"), and 27100 Pacific Coast Highway, Malibu, California 90265 (the \"Malibu Beach House\"), including maintaining all applicable insurance coverage, paying property taxes when due, and arranging for necessary maintenance, repairs, and security;

> \(ii\) The Decedent\'s fifty percent (50%) membership interest in Lumiére Canyon Studios LLC, a California limited liability company (California Secretary of State Filing No. 200906410337), including monitoring the operations and financial performance of the company and exercising the Decedent\'s rights as a member in the ordinary course of business;

> \(iii\) The Decedent\'s thirty-five percent (35%) membership interest in Pacific Rim Narrative Partners LLC, a California limited liability company (California Secretary of State Filing No. 201518720492), including monitoring the operations and financial performance of the company and exercising the Decedent\'s rights as a member in the ordinary course of business;

> \(iv\) Financial accounts held at Veltara Basin Bank, N.A., including the brokerage account ending in -4782, the checking account ending in -3091, and the money market account ending in -6155, and any other accounts identified during the course of administration;

> \(v\) The intellectual property portfolio, consisting of royalties and residuals associated with fourteen (14) feature films and six (6) television series, as more particularly described in Exhibit A;
> \(vi\) Personal property of the Decedent, including art, vehicles, and furnishings, as inventoried by the Neutral Administrator.

> \(b\) **Collection of Income.** Collect all income, rents, royalties, residuals, distributions, dividends, interest, and other amounts attributable to Estate assets in the ordinary course of business, and deposit all such amounts into an Estate account or accounts maintained by the Neutral Administrator at Veltara Basin Bank, N.A., or such other financial institution as the Neutral Administrator may determine to be appropriate.

> \(c\) **Payment of Expenses.** Pay ordinary and necessary expenses of the Estate in the ordinary course, including but not limited to real property taxes, homeowners\' insurance premiums, property maintenance costs, utility bills, vehicle insurance and registration fees, storage fees, professional fees incurred in the ordinary course of Estate administration, and any other expenses reasonably necessary to preserve and protect Estate assets.

> \(d\) **Tax Compliance.** Prepare, or cause to be prepared, and timely file all required federal, state, and local tax returns for the Estate, including but not limited to fiduciary income tax returns (IRS Form 1041 and California Form 541), in coordination with Ridgeway Accounting Partners LLP (Dennis Chua, CPA), with offices at 515 South Flower Street, Suite 3600, Los Angeles, California 90071. The Neutral Administrator shall provide copies of all draft tax returns to Petitioner\'s Counsel and Contestants\' Counsel for review and comment at least fifteen (15) days prior to the applicable filing deadline.

> \(e\) **Quarterly Reporting.** Provide detailed quarterly written reports to Petitioner\'s Counsel and Contestants\' Counsel, with copies to both Petitioner and Contestants upon request, detailing the status of all Estate assets, all income received, all expenses paid, all distributions made (if any), and any material developments relating to the Estate or its assets. Such reports shall be delivered within thirty (30) days following the end of each calendar quarter during the Standstill Period, with the first such report covering the period from the Effective Date through June 30, 2023.

**Section 3.3 --- Restrictions on the Neutral Administrator.** During the Standstill Period, the Neutral Administrator shall not, without the prior written consent of all Parties or further order of the Court, take any of the following actions:

> \(a\) Sell, transfer, convey, assign, exchange, encumber, pledge, hypothecate, lease (other than short-term leases of ninety (90) days or less on terms consistent with prior practice), or otherwise dispose of any Estate asset, whether real, personal, tangible, or intangible;

> \(b\) Make any distribution from the Estate to any Party, any beneficiary, any heir, or any third party, other than payments of ordinary and necessary expenses of administration as described in Section 3.2(c);

> \(c\) Enter into any contract, agreement, commitment, or arrangement on behalf of the Estate that involves consideration, obligations, or exposure exceeding Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$25,000) in value, whether in a single transaction or a series of related transactions;

> \(d\) Incur, assume, guaranty, or otherwise become obligated for any indebtedness on behalf of the Estate, including but not limited to loans, lines of credit, promissory notes, or credit agreements.

For the avoidance of doubt, the restrictions set forth in this Section 3.3 are not intended to prevent the Neutral Administrator from taking emergency actions necessary to protect Estate assets from imminent loss or destruction, provided that the Neutral Administrator shall promptly notify all Parties and their counsel of any such emergency action taken.

**Section 3.4 --- Administration Fees and Costs.** The Neutral Administrator shall be compensated for its services at the rate of Eight Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$8,500) per month, plus fifteen one-hundredths of one percent (0.15%) of assets under administration per annum (the \"AUA Fee\"), as set forth in the Stipulation for Appointment of Neutral Administrator. Such fees and costs shall be allocated and paid as follows:
> \(a\) **Petitioner\'s Share.** Petitioner shall pay Four Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$4,250) per month toward the monthly administration fee.
> \(b\) **Contestants\' Share.** Contestants shall pay, jointly and severally, Four Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$4,250) per month toward the monthly administration fee.

> \(c\) **Timing of Payments.** Monthly fee payments shall be made directly to the Neutral Administrator by the fifth (5th) business day of each calendar month during the Standstill Period. The first monthly payment shall be due on or before the fifth (5th) business day of May 2023.

> \(d\) **AUA Fee.** The per-annum AUA Fee (0.15% of assets under administration) shall be calculated on a quarterly basis using the fair market value of assets under administration as of the last day of the applicable calendar quarter, as determined by the Neutral Administrator in its reasonable judgment. The AUA Fee shall be invoiced quarterly and shall be payable within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of the Neutral Administrator\'s invoice. The AUA Fee shall be allocated equally between Petitioner and Contestants.

> \(e\) **Reimbursable Costs.** In addition to the fees set forth above, the Neutral Administrator shall be entitled to reimbursement for reasonable out-of-pocket costs incurred in the performance of its duties, including but not limited to costs of insurance, appraisals, professional consultants, legal counsel to the Neutral Administrator, postage, filing fees, and travel. All reimbursable costs exceeding Five Thousand Dollars (\$5,000) in any calendar quarter shall require prior notice to Petitioner\'s Counsel and Contestants\' Counsel.

**Section 3.5 --- Failure to Pay Administration Fees.** If either Petitioner or Contestants (treated as a group for purposes of this Section) fails to timely pay its share of the Neutral Administrator\'s monthly fees for two (2) consecutive months, the non-defaulting Party shall have the following remedies, exercisable in its sole discretion:

> \(a\) **Advancement.** The non-defaulting Party may advance the defaulting Party\'s share of the fees directly to the Neutral Administrator, and the amount so advanced shall be treated as an administrative expense of the Estate and shall be reimbursed to the advancing Party from the Estate prior to any distribution to the defaulting Party, with interest at the rate of five percent (5%) per annum from the date of each advancement until repaid; or

> \(b\) **Termination.** The non-defaulting Party may terminate this Agreement upon ten (10) days\' prior written notice to the defaulting Party, delivered in accordance with Section 7.3. The defaulting Party shall have the right to cure the default by paying all arrearages, including any late fees, within the ten (10)-day notice period, in which case the termination notice shall be deemed withdrawn and this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect.
**[ARTICLE IV --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Confidentiality of Settlement Discussions.** All Settlement Discussions between or among the Parties, their respective counsel, the Mediator, or any other person participating in settlement negotiations at the direction of the Parties, whether occurring before, on, or after the Effective Date and during the Standstill Period, shall be and remain strictly confidential. No Party shall disclose, publish, disseminate, or communicate the substance, content, terms, or status of any Settlement Discussion to any person or entity that is not a Party to this Agreement, nor to any attorney, advisor, consultant, expert, or other agent of any Party not directly involved in the Settlement Discussions, without the prior written consent of all other Parties. The foregoing prohibition shall not apply to disclosures required by applicable law, regulation, court order, or subpoena, provided that the disclosing Party shall provide prompt written notice to all other Parties prior to making any such required disclosure and shall cooperate in seeking a protective order or other appropriate remedy to limit the scope of such disclosure.

**Section 4.2 --- Inadmissibility.** All Settlement Discussions, and all documents, communications, proposals, counterproposals, memoranda, position statements, term sheets, draft agreements, and other materials prepared or exchanged in connection with Settlement Discussions, shall be inadmissible in any judicial, arbitral, administrative, or other proceeding, whether pending or future, for any purpose, including but not limited to proof of liability, fault, the validity or invalidity of any claim or defense, or the amount of any damages or award. The inadmissibility protections set forth in this Section 4.2 are intended to be in addition to, and not in limitation of, the protections afforded by California Evidence Code Section 1152 (compromise offers and negotiations), Federal Rule of Evidence 408 (compromise offers and negotiations), and California Evidence Code Sections 1115 through 1128 (mediation confidentiality), all of which the Parties expressly invoke and rely upon. No Party shall seek to compel the Mediator or any other neutral to testify regarding any Settlement Discussion.

**Section 4.3 --- Confidential Information.** All financial information, valuation data, appraisal reports, business records, tax returns, operating statements, balance sheets, membership interest agreements, intellectual property schedules, and other non-public information exchanged between or among the Parties or their counsel in connection with Settlement Discussions, the mediation process, or this Agreement (collectively, \"**Confidential Information**\") shall be treated as confidential and shall not be used for any purpose other than the Settlement Discussions and the potential resolution of the Proceeding. Upon the termination or expiration of this Agreement, each Party shall, at the request of the producing Party, promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information received from the other Party, provided that counsel for each Party may retain one archival copy of all Confidential Information in its litigation files, subject to the continuing confidentiality obligations of this Article IV.

**Section 4.4 --- Court Filings.** The Parties shall not file this Agreement, any amendment hereto, or any exhibit or attachment hereto with the Court or any other tribunal without the prior written consent of all Parties, except where such filing is required by court order, applicable statute, or applicable rule of court. In the event that filing is required, the filing Party shall first confer with all other Parties regarding the possibility of filing under seal or with appropriate redactions to preserve the confidentiality of Settlement Discussions and Confidential Information.

**Section 4.5 --- Survival.** The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article IV, including without limitation the obligations set forth in Sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, and 4.4, shall survive the termination, expiration, or breach of this Agreement and shall remain in full force and effect indefinitely, unless modified or waived by written agreement of all Parties.
**[ARTICLE V --- TERM, RENEWAL, AND TERMINATION]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Initial Term.** This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date, April 28, 2023, and shall continue in full force and effect until the Initial Expiration Date, October 28, 2023, unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Article V or renewed in accordance with Section 5.2.

**Section 5.2 --- Renewal.** This Agreement may be renewed for successive periods of six (6) calendar months each (each a \"**Renewal Period**\") by mutual written consent of all Parties. The written consent to renew must be executed by all Parties, or by their authorized counsel on their behalf, not later than five (5) business days prior to the then-applicable Expiration Date. Each renewal shall be documented by a written amendment to this Agreement signed by all Parties or their authorized counsel, which amendment shall specify the new Expiration Date and any modifications to the terms of this Agreement agreed upon in connection with such renewal. In the absence of a timely written renewal, this Agreement shall expire on the then-applicable Expiration Date without further action by any Party.

**Section 5.3 --- Termination by Mutual Consent.** This Agreement may be terminated at any time, including prior to the Expiration Date, by written agreement of all Parties. Such written agreement shall specify the effective date of termination and shall address any transitional matters, including the recommencement of tolled deadlines and the continued role of the Neutral Administrator.

**Section 5.4 --- Termination by Unilateral Notice.** Any Party may terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to all other Parties and their counsel, delivered in accordance with Section 7.3 of this Agreement. Following delivery of such notice, the Standstill Period shall continue in full force and effect for the thirty (30)-day notice period, and all obligations of the Parties under this Agreement shall remain binding during such period. All tolled deadlines shall recommence on the day immediately following the expiration of the thirty (30)-day notice period. The terminating Party shall act in good faith in exercising its right under this Section 5.4 and shall not terminate this Agreement for the purpose of gaining a tactical advantage in the Proceeding.

**Section 5.5 --- Effect of Termination or Expiration.** Upon the termination or expiration of this Agreement, whether by mutual consent, unilateral notice, lapse of the Standstill Period, or otherwise, the following provisions shall apply:

> \(a\) **Recommencement of Deadlines.** All litigation deadlines tolled pursuant to Section 2.1 shall recommence with the same number of days remaining as existed on the Effective Date, calculated from the date of termination or expiration, as provided in Sections 2.1 and 5.4;

> \(b\) **Survival of Confidentiality Obligations.** All obligations of the Parties under Article IV (Confidentiality) shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement and shall remain in full force and effect in accordance with Section 4.5;

> \(c\) **Continuation of Neutral Administrator.** The Neutral Administrator shall continue to serve in its capacity as neutral administrator of the Estate until further order of the Court or written agreement of all Parties providing for the appointment of a successor or the assumption of administrative duties by a court-appointed personal representative;

> \(d\) **Preservation of Claims and Defenses.** No Party shall be deemed to have waived, released, abandoned, or prejudiced any claim, defense, right, or remedy by virtue of entering into, performing under, or terminating or permitting the expiration of this Agreement. All claims, defenses, rights, and remedies of the Parties as of the Effective Date, and as may have accrued during the Standstill Period, are expressly reserved and preserved.

{"file_path":"response.md","content":"# Largest executed settlement

## Answer

The largest settlement is **$87,500,000** in **_Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al._, Case No. 1021-00006**, in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida (workspace matter **1021-00006**).

The matter concerned alleged underreporting of gross room revenue and resulting unpaid franchise royalties, marketing-fund contributions, technology fees, interest, and related claims across Coastal Palms's hotel franchise portfolio. Verimark's complaint claimed approximately $150 million, and Coastal Palms asserted a $12 million counterclaim. The parties mediated after a partial summary-judgment ruling and executed the final settlement agreement on **April 22, 2024**.

## Why $87.5 million is the correct number

The controlling document is:

- `documents/matters/1021-00006/Mediation & Settlement/final-settlement-agreement-execution.docx`

This document is expressly labeled **“Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (Execution Version)”** and identifies the action and case number. Its operative provisions provide:

- Section 1.22 defines **“Settlement Amount”** as **$87,500,000**.
- Section 2.1 says the parties are settling all claims, counterclaims, and disputes for that total amount.
- The amount consists of a **$25,000,000 initial payment** plus **$62,500,000** in eight structured principal payments of $7,812,500 each.
- The signed payment schedule repeats that the Settlement Amount is $87,500,000.

The agreement's payment schedule estimates total payments of **$96,717,842.47 including interest**. I did **not** use that larger figure because the agreement defines the settlement itself as $87,500,000; the additional amount is estimated interest on deferred structured payments, not a larger defined settlement amount. I likewise did not count the $150 million complaint demand or the $12 million counterclaim as settlement values.

## Cross-check against other executed resolutions

I screened the settlement-related materials and compared the operative executed or execution-version agreements, rather than treating drafts, redlines, offers, term sheets, or settlement-authority memoranda as completed settlements. The other largest executed resolutions located were below $87.5 million, including:

| Matter | Executed document | Defined or operative resolution amount |
|---|---|---:|
| 1021-00003 — _Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Ironclad Indemnity Corp., et al._ | `Mediation & Settlement/settlement-agreement-mutual-release.docx` | **$47,300,000** aggregate Settlement Amount |
| 1027-00003 — _Meridian Shores Hospitality LLC v. Pellegrino Capital Group LLC_ arbitration | `Transaction Documents/mutual-release-and-settlement-agreement.docx` plus the contemporaneous Redemption Agreement | **$52,850,000** Redemption Price used to resolve the dispute |
| 1033-00006 — RGC reporting/media-liability action | `Settlement Documents/settlement-agreement-execution.docx` | **$14,750,000** Settlement Amount |
| 1017-00004 — Aurelius Media California employment class/PAGA action | `Mediation & Settlement/Class Action/class-settlement-agreement-execution.docx` | **$14,750,000** Gross Settlement Amount |
| 1006-00004 — CPS trade-secret action | `Settlement/settlement-agreement-execution.docx` | **$9,750,000** Payment Amount |
| 1038-00006 — Cascade/Verdana trade-secret action | `Settlement & Standstill/standstill-settlement-agreement-execution.docx` | **$8,750,000** defined Settlement Payment, plus a separate $425,000 cost reimbursement |

For the $47.3 million insurance settlement, the executed agreement specifically allocates the amount among four insurers ($24.5 million, $12.2 million, $6.8 million, and $3.8 million), confirming that it is one aggregate settlement rather than four separate settlements. That matter therefore remains well below the $87.5 million Coastal Palms resolution.

## Conclusion

For pitch purposes, the supportable lead figure is:

> **$87.5 million — _Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al._ (Matter 1021-00006).**

That figure follows the executed agreement's defined **Settlement Amount**, without inflating it with projected interest, the amount claimed in the complaint, collateral values, or other amounts mentioned elsewhere in the documents."}

lines.text: # Largest executed settlement
## Answer

The largest settlement is **$87,500,000** in **_Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al._, Case No. 1021-00006**, in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida (workspace matter **1021-00006**).

The matter concerned alleged underreporting of gross room revenue and resulting unpaid franchise royalties, marketing-fund contributions, technology fees, interest, and related claims across Coastal Palms's hotel franchise portfolio. Verimark's complaint claimed approximately $150 million, and Coastal Palms asserted a $12 million counterclaim. The parties mediated after a partial summary-judgment ruling and executed the final settlement agreement on **April 22, 2024**.
## Why $87.5 million is the correct number
The controlling document is:
- `documents/matters/1021-00006/Mediation & Settlement/final-settlement-agreement-execution.docx`
This document is expressly labeled **“Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (Execution Version)”** and identifies the action and case number. Its operative provisions provide:
- Section 1.22 defines **“Settlement Amount”** as **$87,500,000**.
- Section 2.1 says the parties are settling all claims, counterclaims, and disputes for that total amount.
- The amount consists of a **$25,000,000 initial payment** plus **$62,500,000** in eight structured principal payments of $7,812,500 each.
- The signed payment schedule repeats that the Settlement Amount is $87,500,000.

The agreement's payment schedule estimates total payments of **$96,717,842.47 including interest**. I did **not** use that larger figure because the agreement defines the settlement itself as $87,500,000; the additional amount is estimated interest on deferred structured payments, not a larger defined settlement amount. I likewise did not count the $150 million complaint demand or the $12 million counterclaim as settlement values.
## Cross-check against other executed resolutions

I screened the settlement-related materials and compared the operative executed or execution-version agreements, rather than treating drafts, redlines, offers, term sheets, or settlement-authority memoranda as completed settlements. The other largest executed resolutions located were below $87.5 million, including:
| Matter | Executed document | Defined or operative resolution amount |

| 1021-00003 — _Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Ironclad Indemnity Corp., et al._ | `Mediation & Settlement/settlement-agreement-mutual-release.docx` | **$47,300,000** aggregate Settlement Amount |

| 1027-00003 — _Meridian Shores Hospitality LLC v. Pellegrino Capital Group LLC_ arbitration | `Transaction Documents/mutual-release-and-settlement-agreement.docx` plus the contemporaneous Redemption Agreement | **$52,850,000** Redemption Price used to resolve the dispute |
| 1033-00006 — RGC reporting/media-liability action | `Settlement Documents/settlement-agreement-execution.docx` | **$14,750,000** Settlement Amount |
| 1017-00004 — Aurelius Media California employment class/PAGA action | `Mediation & Settlement/Class Action/class-settlement-agreement-execution.docx` | **$14,750,000** Gross Settlement Amount |
| 1006-00004 — CPS trade-secret action | `Settlement/settlement-agreement-execution.docx` | **$9,750,000** Payment Amount |

| 1038-00006 — Cascade/Verdana trade-secret action | `Settlement & Standstill/standstill-settlement-agreement-execution.docx` | **$8,750,000** defined Settlement Payment, plus a separate $425,000 cost reimbursement |

For the $47.3 million insurance settlement, the executed agreement specifically allocates the amount among four insurers ($24.5 million, $12.2 million, $6.8 million, and $3.8 million), confirming that it is one aggregate settlement rather than four separate settlements. That matter therefore remains well below the $87.5 million Coastal Palms resolution.
## Conclusion
For pitch purposes, the supportable lead figure is:
> **$87.5 million — _Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al._ (Matter 1021-00006).**

That figure follows the executed agreement's defined **Settlement Amount**, without inflating it with projected interest, the amount claimed in the complaint, collateral values, or other amounts mentioned elsewhere in the documents.
